 iPhone Price Increase Lifts Overall Revenue
Greater China Sales Fall Short of Market Expectations
 International | Published 2026.11.03. 07:05:53 | By Kim Chang-young kcy@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A John Ternus, Apple's chief executive officer. Reuters-Yonhap News SILICON VALLEY — Apple delivered results in line with market expectations in its first quarterly earnings report since replacing its chief executive, but showed weakness in its China business. New products including the iPhone 18 series helped offset the shock from surging memory prices, though sales in China, one of Apple's largest markets, fell short of expectations.
 Apple said on the 2nd that revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter, covering July through September, rose 12% from a year earlier to $114.48 billion. The figure topped Bloomberg's estimate of $113.47 billion. Earnings per share came in at $2.10, beating analysts' estimates of $2. Gross margin was 47.9%, above the 47.5% Wall Street consensus compiled by London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG).
 iPhone revenue, the largest component of Apple's product sales, reached $57.58 billion, exceeding estimates of $56.49 billion. Analysts called the result solid given that only eight days of sales from the iPhone 18 series, launched at the end of the quarter, were reflected. The iPhone Duo, Apple's foldable model, was released in October and was not included. As component prices soared amid the memory supply crunch, Apple raised the launch price of its new iPhone by $100 from the previous model, which analysts said lifted iPhone revenue above market expectations. Gross margin stood at 47.9%.
 Greater China revenue, however, came in at just $17.54 billion, below estimates of $18.75 billion. Greater China is one of Apple's key sales markets. iPad sales were also weak, totaling $6.23 billion against Wall Street estimates of $6.83 billion.
